text:
pagerduty-bot: URGENT: P1 - elevated reconnects + 5xx for some customers in us-west-2 (az3). Symptoms: increased TCP retransmits, IPv6 flows failing, DNS retries. Alert: net.retransmit.rate > 15% for 10m. INC-2026-01234 created.

oncall-elena: got the page, looking now. can someone grab tcpdump on the edge lb? 

samir: I can. starting capture on lb-edge-usw2a-03. running: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s0 -w /tmp/edge-usw2a.pcap host 2001:db8::/32 or host 10.0.0.0/8

liz: quick q — are we seeing IPv4 degraded too or just v6? metrics show spikes only on v6 paths so far.

oncall-elena: confirmed — v6 only so far. IPv4 looks fine. that suggests path MTU or ICMP blocking in one AZ.

networking-ng: noticed BGP multi-exit point changes earlier today for az3, possible ECMP asymmetry. weaving those notes in.

samir: tcpdump shows lots of ICMPv6 "packet too big" messages but they're not getting to origin, looks like they get dropped at the tenant edge appliance. traceroute6 from probe: 
```
traceroute6 -n -w 1 -m 30 2606:4700::6810:xxxx
1  2001:db8::1  1.23 ms
2  2606:4700::1  1.56 ms
3  * * *   (no ICMP responses)
```

oncall-elena: that matches PMTUD failure — fragment/jumbo negotiation likely failing at az3 edge hw. impact: several customers report failed uploads and DNS timeouts when client prefers v6. CS has 5 reports so far.

customer-success-jamie: FYI customers affected: AcmeAnalytics (uploads failing), BrightForms (api POSTs 502), two CDN partners intermittently failing. All opened tickets.

infra-bot: Suggest mitigation options: 1) enable MSS clamping on ingress LB for TCP SYNs 2) temporarily prefer IPv4 via DNS or BGP 3) push MTU clamp on edge appliances.

oncall-elena: let's try MSS clamping first (least invasive). applying on lb-edge-usw2a-03: 
```
# on linux LB
iptables -t mangle -A PREROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
applying now.

samir: applied on two active LBs in az3. will monitor.

liz: telemetry shows retransmit rate dropping from 18% -> 6% within 90s. DNS retry rate also improving.

networking-ng: good. still seeing some downstream appliances dropping ICMPv6 PTB. plan: escalate to hw vendor to patch jumbo negotiation logic on those blades; logging a ticket.

oncall-elena: for customers still impacted we'll offer temporary IPv4 fallback. jamie can you prepare a short CS note? include workaround: disable IPv6 on client, or use our v4 endpoint.

customer-success-jamie: drafting now. message: "We're aware of packet-size related IPv6 failures in us-west-2 az3 causing intermittent uploads. We're applying MTU/MSS workarounds; temporary IPv4 endpoint available. ETA to full fix: we're coordinating with networking vendor, updates in 1h." want to include technical details?

oncall-elena: short and clear. include that we've applied MSS clamp and are monitoring; no data loss, just increased retries/timeouts.

samir: handing off monitoring duty to liz (next shift) — I'll stay on vendor call for firmware trace. 

oncall-elena: handing to samir for vendor, liz you're on-monitor until 1932113476. notes: check edge counters, ICMPv6 PTB sent/received, customer tickets.

infra-bot: Checklist updated in INC-2026-01234: mitigation applied (MSS clamp), vendor ticket opened (VND-7892), CS note posted, monitoring thresholds lowered.

liz: ACK. setting alert to watch 5xx > 1% for 5m on v6-only paths. will post updates if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

networking-ng: vendor responded — their 2.3.1 firmware has a jumbo-negotiation race on certain ASICs; patch ETA 48h, hotfix in-progress. we asked for emergency micropatch.

customer-success-jamie: posted to affected customers with workaround and contact. one partner requested SLA credit — routing to account team.

oncall-elena: summary for incident log: root cause suspected: edge appliance fails to forward ICMPv6 "Packet Too Big" (PMTUD) for jumbo/large frames under certain ECMP path asymmetry in az3. mitigation: MSS clamping on LBs reduced impact; vendor engagement ongoing for firmware fix. impact: intermittent uploads/503s for IPv6-preferring clients, ~2-4% of overall traffic in the region, ~7 reported customer tickets. next steps: monitor + vendor patch + planned rolling reconfiguration to clamp MTU at edge if micropatch delayed.

samir: leaving vendor call notes in the ticket. I'll update timeline if hotfix arrives.

liz: monitoring green for now. closing the active paging loop but keeping incident open for vendor patch.

oncall-elena: thanks all — nice quick mitigation. :clap:
